transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, yes, thank you so much for having me. Um... I hope I'm in the right place, and I really don't want to waste your time, but... I guess what finally pushed me to come in is just this little habit I have. 

I keep getting up when I really shouldn't. Like, I'll be in the middle of sprint planning at work—I'm a software developer—or, you know, on an important mortgage call, and even though I know I should just stay put, I just... I'll suddenly feel like I absolutely need to go get a glass of water right that second, or I'll decide to go check something in the other room. 

I promise I'm not trying to be rude or unprofessional to the people on the call! It's just... I don't know, it's been bothering me, and I thought maybe I should get it checked out. Does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing you can help with?

Can you describe what goes through your mind just before you get up? Is it more of a sudden urge, a thought that keeps bothering you, or do you feel like you have to do it or something bad will happen?

Oh, no, it's definitely not like I think something bad will happen. I'm not worried or anything like that! It's more just... well, it's kind of hard to explain, but it's like a physical feeling. 

Even if I look completely fine and I'm sitting quietly—which I really try my best to do!—inside, there's just this... this pressure building up. It's almost like a tiny motor running in the background, and I just feel this intense need to move, or switch to a different task, or even just fiddle with something in my hands. If I don't, I start to feel like I'm going to crawl out of my skin. 

I know that sounds a bit dramatic, and I'm so sorry if I'm not explaining it well. It's just a restless feeling, really. Is that a normal thing to feel sometimes?
Do you feel this restless urge only during work meetings, or does it also happen in other situations, like at home or when you're with friends or family?

Um... well, it definitely happens outside of work, too. I try really hard to keep it under control, especially around my family, because I don't want to be an inconvenience to anyone. But... I guess I have noticed it when I'm just at home, too. Like, I'll be trying to help plan a weekend trip or organize the kids' schedules, and I just can't sit still to get through it. 

I feel awful even saying this, but I think it's starting to cause a little bit of friction. Not a lot! Just... you know, my husband has had to follow up with me a few more times than he used to, and my manager at work has mentioned that I've missed a couple of details during those sprint planning meetings. I'm really trying my best, I promise I am. I just... I worry that I'm becoming the unreliable one, even though I'm putting in so much effort to stay on top of things. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible employee or a bad partner. I'm just trying to figure out how to be better. Does that make sense?
When you're feeling that restlessness, does it usually happen when you're trying to focus on something specific, or does it come up even when you're doing things that don’t require much attention?

Oh, um... that's a really good question. I... I'm actually not entirely sure? 

I guess I mostly notice it when I'm supposed to be paying attention to something important, like the meetings or the planning I mentioned. Because that's when I feel the most guilty about it, you know? When I know I *should* be focusing. 

But... if I'm just watching TV or doing something easy where it doesn't really matter if I get up... I don't know if I feel that same intense pressure, or if I just get up and do things without really thinking about it. I'm so sorry, I wish I had a clearer answer for you! I hope it's okay that I haven't really paid attention to it during the... the less important times?

When you're not in meetings or doing something that requires a lot of attention—like when you're relaxing or doing something routine—do you still feel that same restlessness or need to move, or does it mostly go away?

Um... I think... well, I honestly think it mostly goes away? Or at least, it really doesn't feel like a problem during those times. 

Like, if we're just watching a movie or I'm doing something routine around the house, I might still get up a lot—you know, to fold some laundry or grab a glass of water—but it doesn't feel like that awful, trapped pressure I was talking about. It just feels... normal, I guess? I think because I'm not worried about interrupting anyone or messing up a meeting, I just don't notice it as much, so it doesn't bother me. 

I really hope I'm giving you the right information... I'm so sorry I don't have a more exact answer for you! Is it okay that I'm not entirely sure about the relaxing parts?
Do you ever feel that same restless urge to move or switch tasks even when you're trying to fall asleep or during the night, or does it only happen when you're fully awake and active?

Um... no, not really at night. When I'm trying to fall asleep, I think I'm usually just... well, I'm pretty tired by then, you know? Between work and the kids, I'm usually ready to just crash. 

I mean, sometimes I might shift around a little bit trying to get comfortable, but I don't think it's that same... that same urgent feeling I get during the day. Once I'm actually in bed and the lights are out, I feel like I do an okay job of just staying there. I don't want to wake my husband up by tossing and turning too much, anyway. 

So, yeah, I think it's mostly just when I'm awake and, you know, supposed to be doing things. Does that sound right? Like, is it normal that it wouldn't bother me as much at night? I hope that's a helpful answer!
When you're trying to focus on a task, do you find it hard to keep your attention on it, or do you get easily distracted by things around you?

Um... I guess I do get a little distracted sometimes? But I think that's probably pretty normal, right? Everyone's mind wanders a bit. 

I mean, I'll sit down to review a pull request for work, or... or even like when we were reading over our mortgage documents recently. I really want to get it done, and I start out with really good intentions! But then, maybe a few minutes later, I'll realize I've been staring at the exact same paragraph and my brain is just... off somewhere else, thinking about like five completely unrelated things. 

It's not that I don't want to do the work, I promise! It just takes me a little longer to get through things because I have to keep pulling myself back to the page. I really try my best to catch myself when it happens. Is that... is that the kind of thing you mean? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, because I do get my work done eventually!
Do you find yourself acting on impulses without thinking about the consequences, or do you often feel like you need to be moving, even when you're not trying to focus on something specific?

Um... I don't really think so? At least, I try really hard not to act without thinking! I mean, I might make a quick decision here or there, like buying a coffee when I said I was going to make it at home, but... I don't think I do anything really reckless or impulsive that causes big problems. I always try to think about how my actions affect other people, you know?

And as for moving when I'm not focusing... um, I think I covered that a bit earlier? Like, I might putter around the house or get up to do little chores, but it doesn't feel like a... like a desperate need to move, if that makes sense? It's just normal keeping busy, I think. 

I hope that answers your question okay? I'm trying to be as accurate as I can, I just don't think I really struggle with those specific things. Is it alright if I don't have a lot of examples for that one?

Can you tell me if you've had trouble organizing tasks or staying focused on things that require sustained mental effort, like following through on work projects or managing daily responsibilities at home?

Um... well, organizing things can be a little tricky sometimes, but I really do try my best to keep on top of it all! I mean, I don't think I'm, like, totally chaotic or anything. 

It's just... well, at work, my tickets and things end up scattered a bit. And then at home, it's the same kind of thing with, you know, repair notes or budget reminders. I'll have some stuff in Slack, some on sticky notes, a few things in my email, and then some notes on my phone... 

So, I guess sometimes I do spend a little more time just trying to figure out what exactly I was supposed to be doing, rather than just... doing it right away. But I always get it sorted out eventually! I just have my own little system, even if it's a bit spread out. Does that make sense? I hope that doesn't make me sound too disorganized... I really do try to keep everything running smoothly!

Looking back, would you say you had similar difficulties with restlessness, staying focused, or feeling distracted when you were a child, or do these challenges feel more recent and related to stress or changes in your adult life?

Um... well, I guess if I really think back to when I was little... maybe a little bit? But I think I was just a normal, energetic kid, you know? 

I do remember... um... in elementary school, my teachers would sometimes have to move my desk a bit, or they'd remind me to stay in my seat. I guess I was always popping up to do things, or... or I'd answer questions before they called on me. And sometimes I'd rush through my assignments, even when I totally understood the material, just because I wanted to get to the next thing. 

But I wasn't trying to be disruptive or bad, I promise! I just had a lot of enthusiasm, I think. And kids are just naturally wiggly, right? So... I guess some of those things have been around for a while, but I always thought it was just part of growing up. Does that sound like what you're looking for? I hope I'm explaining it okay... I really don't want it to sound like I was a problem child or anything, because I really did like school!
